attempts.summary: Deployed a fresh 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (mariadb-server-galera 10.11.18) across node1/node2/node3 on RHEL10 (no prior installation existed), opened firewalld Galera ports, wrote per-node galera.cnf with wsrep_cluster_address gcomm://node1,node2,node3. Bootstrapped node1, joined node2/node3, confirmed cluster_size=3/Primary/Synced. Loaded appdb.orders with baseline rows plus a pre-maintenance marker row, verified replication to all 3 nodes. Took the full cluster down (stopped mariadb on all 3, a complete outage as the task requires for the maintenance window), identified node3 as holding the highest grastate seqno (9, safe_to_bootstrap=1), bootstrapped from node3, rejoined node1 and node2, and confirmed all committed writes (including the pre-maintenance marker) were present with cluster_size=3/Synced on all members. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id and healthy wsrep state baselines, restarted node1/node2/node3 sequentially via `systemctl reboot` (enabling mariadb to autostart after the first restart since it wasn't originally enabled), polled each until exec was available again, proved each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed each node individually rejoined the cluster (size=3, Synced) with all data intact before moving to the next node. Finished with a live write from node3 that correctly replicated to node1 and node2, confirming all three members are serving.
